title: The Border of Marseille's old port
premise: Ansel Yarrow, a former intelligence analyst fired from three agencies after a botched operation she still can't remember clearly, is living in a Marseille safe house when a real-estate listing appears online showing the interior — including her things and a figure in her window. The listing is a message from the Vasilov network, announcing that they know where the defector she once protected is hiding. Ansel must smuggle the defector, Ilse Brandt, out of the old port before the EU summit, but every ally she recruits is compromised, and Ilse herself may be deliberate bait designed to lure Ansel into the open. In the end Ansel realizes the listing was created by her old handler to force her back into service, sacrifices her chance at reinstatement to expose him publicly, and escapes with Ilse and a makeshift crew of port workers who become the family she never had.
about_author: Bram Dunmore is a former maritime journalist who spent a decade filing dispatches from Mediterranean port cities before turning to fiction. He writes thrillers about people the system has chewed up and quietly discarded.

chapters.title: The Listing
chapters.summary: Ansel's POV. Insomniac Ansel spots a property listing for her own safe house, complete with photos of her bedroom and a blurred figure at the window. She verifies the photos were taken in the last 48 hours. The chapter establishes her paranoia, her routine, and the cold drop of realization: someone is watching, and they want her to know it. Emotional beat: dread sharpening into focus.

chapters.title: Salt and Rust
chapters.summary: Ansel's POV. She works the old port's margins — a fishmonger who owes her, a dockworker named Théo with a boat — to trace who photographed the house. She finds the photographer's abandoned camera and a memory card containing surveillance of Ilse Brandt, the defector she extracted three years ago and believed dead. Emotional beat: guilt resurfacing; the past is not past.

chapters.title: The Woman in the Chapel
chapters.summary: Alternating POV, Ansel and Ilse. Ansel tracks Ilse to a deconsecrated chapel near Panier and finds her alive, hiding under a false name, terrified. Ilse insists she never contacted anyone, but her old codes appear in the listing's metadata. Ansel must decide whether Ilse is a victim or the lure. Emotional beat: wary reunion, trust as a calculated risk.

chapters.title: Three Names, Three Wrecks
chapters.summary: Ilse's POV. Ilse recounts the operation that destroyed Ansel's career — and reveals a detail Ansel has never remembered: the incident wasn't an accident, it was authorized. The chapter deepens the theme of identity as Ansel confronts that her memory was edited, not failed. Emotional beat: the floor dropping out of Ansel's self-narrative.

chapters.title: The Summit Clock
chapters.summary: Ansel's POV. With the summit ten days out, security sweeps of Marseille intensify, and both women realize Ilse's knowledge of the Vasilov network makes her a prize every agency wants — dead or alive. Ansel reaches out to her former handler, Marcus Reeve, against her better judgment. He offers extraction and protection. Emotional beat: hope that tastes like a trap.

chapters.title: Théo's Boat
chapters.summary: Théo's POV. The dockworker, drawn into the plan, ferries the women by night to a staging cove and reveals he has his own history with men who operate outside the law — his brother disappeared into a Vasilov ship years ago. The found-family theme crystallizes: strangers choosing each other over institutions. Emotional beat: solidarity forged in salt water.

chapters.title: Compromised
chapters.summary: Ansel's POV. The safe extraction route collapses — a port authority contact sells them out, and a hit team nearly takes Ilse at the fish market. Ansel realizes only three people knew the route, and one of them is Reeve. The listing, she now suspects, was never from Vasilov at all. Emotional beat: betrayal confirmed; paranoia becomes certainty.

chapters.title: The Bait Before the Summit
chapters.summary: Ilse's POV. Ilse confesses: Reeve contacted her months ago and she fled him too. She was the bait all along, dangled to draw Ansel out of hiding because Ansel's fragmented memory contains the only evidence of Reeve's authorization of the original incident. The summit is Reeve's deadline to erase them both. Emotional beat: terror transformed into resolve.

chapters.title: Old Port, New Reckoning
chapters.summary: Ansel's POV, climax. During the summit's opening night, Ansel walks into Reeve's meeting under the guise of surrender, wearing a camera and a plan built with Théo, Ilse, and the port's quiet network of the discarded. She triggers a live feed of Reeve's confession — including the memory-edit order — to summit security and press. A chase through the fish market ends with Reeve arrested and Ansel bleeding but upright. Emotional beat: justice seized, not granted.

chapters.title: What the Tide Brings Back
chapters.summary: Ansel's POV, resolution. Weeks later, agencies offer her reinstatement; she declines, choosing the port instead. Ilse takes a new name with Ansel's help, Théo's boat becomes their livelihood, and the safe house is finally, genuinely listed for sale — this time by Ansel, with empty rooms. She sleeps through the night for the first time in years. Emotional beat: found family, and peace earned rather than issued.
